lessons.title: x − 3 = 2
lessons.label: x − 3 = 2
lessons.objective: Use the same inverse operation on both sides to isolate x.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Changing one side alone preserves equality.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must we do the same operation on both sides?

steps.title: Find the value of x
steps.explanation: Our goal is to leave x on its own.
steps.detail: The two sides are equal. Add 3 on both sides to undo subtracting 3.

steps.title: Add 3 on the left
steps.explanation: Add 3 on the left only. The sides are now unequal.
steps.detail: This is an intentionally unequal demonstration, not a valid equation. We must do the same to the right.

steps.title: Add 3 on the right too
steps.explanation: The same operation on both sides restores equality.
steps.detail: The beam is level again. Both new terms have the same purple colour.

steps.title: Opposites make zero
steps.explanation: −3 and +3 cancel: together they make zero.

steps.title: The answer is x = 5
steps.explanation: Adding zero changes nothing. So x = 5.

lessons.title: x + 3 = 2
lessons.label: x + 3 = 2
lessons.objective: Use the same inverse operation on both sides to isolate x.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Changing one side alone preserves equality.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must we do the same operation on both sides?

steps.title: Find the value of x
steps.explanation: Our goal is to leave x on its own.
steps.detail: The two sides are equal. Subtract 3 on both sides to undo adding 3.

steps.title: Subtract 3 on the left
steps.explanation: Subtract 3 on the left only. The sides are now unequal.
steps.detail: This is an intentionally unequal demonstration, not a valid equation. We must do the same to the right.

steps.title: Subtract 3 on the right too
steps.explanation: The same operation on both sides restores equality.
steps.detail: The beam is level again. Both new terms have the same purple colour.

steps.title: Opposites make zero
steps.explanation: +3 and −3 cancel: together they make zero.
steps.detail: On the right, 2 − 3 = −1: start at 2, count back 3, and go one below zero.

steps.title: The answer is x = −1
steps.explanation: Adding zero changes nothing. So x = −1.
steps.detail: A negative answer is allowed. Check: −1 + 3 = 2. Both sides are equal.

lessons.title: 3x = 12
lessons.label: 3x = 12
lessons.objective: Divide both sides into three equal groups.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Dividing only one side, or taking away 3 instead of dividing.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: What happens to each of the twelve units when we divide by three?

steps.title: Three equal x-groups
steps.explanation: 3x means three equal groups of x. Together they equal 12.

steps.title: Split both sides into three groups
steps.explanation: Divide both sides by 3. Share the twelve units equally among the three x-groups.

steps.title: Each x-group contains four
steps.explanation: Each group has one x and four units. So x = 4.

lessons.title: x / 4 = 3
lessons.label: x / 4 = 3
lessons.objective: Rebuild a whole from four equal quarters.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Subtracting four instead of making four equal copies.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do four quarters make x?

steps.title: One quarter of x is three
steps.explanation: A quarter of x is 3. We need four equal quarters to make the whole.

steps.title: Multiply both sides by four
steps.explanation: Make four copies on both sides. Four quarters make one whole x.

steps.title: The whole is twelve
steps.explanation: Four groups of three make twelve. So x = 12.

lessons.title: 2x + 3 = 11
lessons.label: 2x + 3 = 11
lessons.objective: Undo addition, then divide both sides equally.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Dividing only the x term while ignoring the added 3.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why did we subtract 3 before dividing by 2?

steps.title: Undo one operation at a time
steps.explanation: First undo adding 3. Then undo multiplying x by 2.

steps.title: Subtract three on both sides
steps.explanation: Subtract 3 from both sides to keep equality.

steps.title: Cancel opposites
steps.explanation: +3 and −3 make zero. On the right, 11 − 3 = 8.

steps.title: Divide both sides by two
steps.explanation: Share eight units equally between two x-groups.

lessons.title: 3x + 2x = 15
lessons.label: 3x + 2x = 15
lessons.objective: Collect equal x-tiles, then solve by equal grouping.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why can we collect these tiles together?

steps.title: All the tiles represent the same x
steps.explanation: There are three x-tiles and two more x-tiles.

steps.title: Collect the five x-tiles
steps.explanation: 3x + 2x makes 5x. We count five copies of the same unknown.

steps.title: Divide both sides by five
steps.explanation: Split fifteen into five equal groups. Each x-group gets three.

lessons.title: 3(x + 2)
lessons.label: 3(x + 2)
lessons.objective: Expand three copies of a group by distributing to every term.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Multiplying only x and forgetting to multiply the 2.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: How many units are in three copies of x + 2?

steps.title: Three copies of the bracket
steps.explanation: The 3 multiplies the whole group: x and 2.

steps.title: Make all three copies
steps.explanation: Each copy contains one x and two units.

steps.title: Collect the x-tiles
steps.explanation: There are three x-tiles. Keep all six unit tiles.

steps.title: Three lots of two make six
steps.explanation: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6. We cannot find a number for x from this expression alone.
